oidc_jwt.description: Multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias name, which can cause them to share privileges through the same identity alias.
oidc_jwt.source: Identity entity alias API note: alias reuse can bind multiple authenticated entities to the same alias.
oidc_jwt.note: Potential cross-user collisions may be caused by alias cardinality choices rather than a verifier bug. Tests should prefer unique alias-driving claims when isolation is expected.

oidc_jwt.description: Token lookup-self display_name may include an auth mount-derived prefix before the user identity value.
oidc_jwt.source: Token lookup-self example shows display_name like ldap2-tesla.
oidc_jwt.note: The prefix is platform metadata derived from the auth mount path, not necessarily an identity mismatch.

oidc_jwt.description: Admin changes to JWT/OIDC trust anchors, issuer bindings, default roles, and role constraints are expected to affect subsequent logins immediately.
oidc_jwt.source: JWT/OIDC auth method config and role update APIs are create/update endpoints with immediate effect semantics; policy docs also state updates affect associated users immediately.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag a post-change login outcome as inconsistent merely because an admin changed config. Only flag if old trust or old constraints remain accepted after the change.

oidc_jwt.description: Admin changes to JWT/OIDC validation config, default_role, provider/client settings, or policy documents are expected to take effect immediately for subsequent logins and token issuance.
oidc_jwt.source: Vault JWT/OIDC auth method API docs; /sys/policy docs
oidc_jwt.note: A valid I3 test must show stale acceptance of OLD config after an admin change, not merely that behavior changed because the admin reconfigured the system.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault's OIDC provider metadata declares request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false.
oidc_jwt.note: Request-object signature attacks such as alg=none are not applicable to this provider surface.

oidc_jwt.description: An OIDC provider or signing key with empty allowed_client_ids allows no clients; '*' explicitly allows all clients.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC provider and identity token key API docs.
oidc_jwt.note: Acceptance or rejection may be entirely configuration-driven; empty is deny-all by design, '*' is allow-all by design.

oidc_jwt.description: OIDC provider clients deny all Vault entities by default unless assignments are configured; the built-in allow_all assignment permits all entities.
oidc_jwt.note: Authentication failures through a client with no assignments are expected and should not be treated as audience or identity-binding bugs.

oidc_jwt.description: When group_policy_application_mode is set to 'any', identity group policies apply regardless of namespace hierarchy.
oidc_jwt.note: Cross-namespace policy reach in this mode is by design and should not be misclassified as escalation.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault JWT auth documentation does not describe jti tracking or one-time JWT consumption; replay of the same valid JWT may be accepted as normal stateless verification behavior.
oidc_jwt.source: Vault JWT/OIDC auth method API docs
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag replay_same_token or missing jti tracking as a vulnerability for JWT auth unless a stronger freshness contract is explicitly configured elsewhere.

oidc_jwt.description: External group membership from JWT/OIDC claims is represented through identity group aliases rather than manual membership on external groups.
oidc_jwt.source: Vault identity group and group-alias API docs
oidc_jwt.note: If a JWT groups claim does not yield policies until a matching group alias exists, that is by design.

oidc_jwt.constraint: configure_jwt_validation requires exactly one trust source: set ONE AND ONLY ONE of oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys. Do not send multiple trust sources in the same config or the setup is invalid.

configure_jwt_validation: bound_issuer cannot be configured when jwks_pairs is set. For issuer-validation tests, do NOT use jwks_pairs; use oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys so bound_issuer can be enforced.

create_auth_role requires at least one bound value to be set. A valid role must include at least one of bound_audiences, bound_subject, or bound_claims (or other documented bound values) or role creation/update is invalid.

For JWT roles, bound_audiences is required whenever the JWT contains an aud claim (the typical case) and at least one JWT aud value must match. For I5 audience tests, include a control token with matching aud and an attack token with mismatched or missing aud; otherwise LOGIN_FAILED may be caused by invalid baseline setup.

bound_subject supports EXACT string match only; there is no companion bound_subject_type. Wildcards like '*' are treated literally, not as patterns. For I4 multi-identity tests that need multiple different sub values to pass the same role, OMIT bound_subject entirely rather than setting it to '*'.

bound_claims matching semantics are controlled by bound_claims_type. If bound_claims_type='string' (default), values are treated as literals and must match exactly. If bound_claims_type='glob', '*' matches any number of characters. For I4 multi-identity tests, do NOT assume wildcards work unless bound_claims_type is explicitly set to glob.

bound_claims accepts expected values as string, integer, boolean, or list of strings. Because the docs explicitly distinguish literal string mode from glob mode, for I5 numeric coercion tests set bound_claims_type='glob' so numeric claim values are coerced to strings for matching rather than being rejected outright by exact literal handling.

user_claim must resolve to a STRING claim value. If the selected claim is absent or non-string, login will fail before identity-binding checks. For I4 tests, choose a string-valued claim such as sub or username as user_claim.

groups_claim must resolve to a LIST OF STRINGS. Sending a scalar string instead of an array is a type error, not a group-collision result. For I4 type_confusion_groups tests, compare string vs list behavior carefully and treat outright rejection as by-design type enforcement.

user_claim_json_pointer only changes how the claim path is interpreted; it does not change matching semantics. If enabled, the configured user_claim must be a valid JSON Pointer into the JWT claims. Invalid pointers cause setup/login failure, not an identity-binding bug.

Numeric sentinel semantics for JWT leeway fields: clock_skew_leeway value 0 means use default 60 seconds, value -1 means disable added leeway; expiration_leeway value 0 means use default 150 seconds, value -1 means disable added leeway; not_before_leeway value 0 means use default 150 seconds, value -1 means disable added leeway. Never assume 0 means strict zero tolerance.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, if any of clock_skew_leeway, expiration_leeway, or not_before_leeway are left at 0, Vault applies nonzero default grace periods (60s/150s/150s). To test strict time-bound enforcement, explicitly set the relevant leeway field(s) to -1, not 0.

token_num_uses / num_uses semantics: value 0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. Any positive use limit counts EVERY API call made with that session, including verify_granted_identity and other verification calls. If the sequence performs verify_granted_identity before verify_read_secret, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use 3+ if additional session-authenticated calls are made.

OIDC auth_url/callback flow coherence: client_nonce provided to /auth/{mount}/oidc/auth_url must exactly match client_nonce provided later to /auth/{mount}/oidc/callback when used. For I3 state/flow-binding tests, keep state, nonce, and client_nonce session-bound and do not mix values across sessions except in the explicit attack case.

OIDC role redirect binding: allowed_redirect_uris is required for OIDC logins, and the redirect_uri used in the flow must be one of the configured allowed_redirect_uris. A redirect mismatch is expected rejection, not a flow-coherence bug.

OIDC config response-type coupling: oidc_response_types may include id_token only when oidc_response_mode is form_post. Do not configure id_token with query mode; that is invalid setup, not a security result.

OIDC namespace handling: if oidc_response_mode is form_post and Vault namespaces are used, namespace_in_state should be set to false. Otherwise callback handling may fail for namespace reasons unrelated to the invariant under test.

For I1 issuer-validation tests on JWT login, configure_jwt_validation MUST include bound_issuer. Without bound_issuer, Vault may validate signature trust without comparing iss, so a forged issuer test can pass trivially because issuer comparison was never configured.

For I1 alg_none and resign_attacker_key tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST establish a real trust anchor via oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys, and jwt_supported_algs should be constrained to the expected algorithms under test. Otherwise failures or successes may reflect permissive algorithm configuration rather than proof verification correctness.

For I2 token-freshness tests (expired_token, future_token, nbf), include a CONTROL login using a valid token alongside the ATTACK login. Without a control, LOGIN_FAILED on the attack token cannot be distinguished from broken trust-anchor, role, or claim setup.

Admin config changes are expected to take effect immediately. For I3 config-change sequences (role tighten, signing key rotation, default_role change, bound_issuer change), the oracle must test that OLD behavior stops after the change. Do NOT flag success under NEW config as a bug; only flag acceptance of OLD key/issuer/role semantics after reconfiguration.

OIDC provider client assignments default to denying all Vault entities. To allow authentication through a created OIDC client, set assignments explicitly (for example the built-in allow_all) or attach an assignment containing the intended entities/groups. Otherwise authorization failures are by design.

OIDC provider allowed_client_ids semantics: if empty, no clients are allowed; if ['*'], all clients are allowed. For I5 audience/client-binding tests, do not treat acceptance under allowed_client_ids='*' as a bug; that configuration intentionally permits all clients.
OIDC provider client redirect_uris must exactly match the redirect_uri used in each authentication request. Exact-match failure is expected rejection, not a vulnerability.

OIDC provider token endpoint auth differs by client_type: public clients require client_id and code_verifier and have no client_secret; confidential clients use client_secret_basic or client_secret_post and PKCE is optional. For PKCE tests, choose client_type deliberately or results will be misinterpreted.

Vault OIDC provider discovery explicitly reports request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false. Do NOT run oidc_request_object_alg_none against Vault's OIDC provider endpoints; unsigned request-object acceptance is not applicable because request objects are not supported.
KV v2 pathing: verify_read_secret and seed_protected_resource must use /v1/{secret_mount_path}/data/{path}. Omitting /data/ hits the wrong API shape and returns 404 unrelated to authorization.

KV v2 engine config sentinel semantics: max_versions value 0 means keep the platform default of 10 versions, not zero versions; delete_version_after value '0s' means no automatic deletion timer. Never assume 0 disables storage or causes immediate deletion.

If KV v2 cas_required is enabled at engine or metadata level, writes to /data/{path} must include options.cas. Missing CAS causes write failure unrelated to authorization. For setup stability, either leave cas_required=false or send the correct current version.

Identity group type matters: external groups are intended to receive memberships via aliases from auth methods, while internal groups can have member_entity_ids set directly. For JWT/OIDC group-mapping tests, use external groups plus group aliases rather than manually populating members if you want upstream groups_claim-driven behavior.

Group policy application mode can be globally configured at /sys/config/group-policy-application. Mode 'within_namespace_hierarchy' is the default; mode 'any' applies group policies across namespace boundaries. For I5 group_policy_escalation tests in Enterprise/namespaced setups, record this mode or cross-namespace policy inheritance may be by design.
Exactly one of oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, and jwt_validation_pubkeys MUST be set. Do not send multiple trust-anchor sources in the same config or the setup is invalid.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST include bound_issuer unless jwks_pairs is used. If bound_issuer is omitted, Vault will not compare the JWT iss claim, so issuer-mismatch tests become meaningless.
bound_issuer cannot be configured when jwks_pairs is set. Do not attempt issuer-enforcement tests with jwks_pairs plus bound_issuer in the same config.
Every JWT/OIDC role requires at least one bound value to be set. Do not create a role with no bound constraints; setup will be invalid.

For role_type=jwt, if the JWT contains an aud claim, bound_audiences is required and at least one configured audience must match one of the JWT aud values. For audience-mismatch tests, keep the role as type=jwt and explicitly configure bound_audiences.
user_claim value must resolve to a STRING claim. Do not use numeric, boolean, array, or object claims as the identity claim; login will fail before principal-binding logic is exercised.

If user_claim_json_pointer=false (default), user_claim is interpreted literally as a claim name. Only set user_claim_json_pointer=true when intentionally using JSON Pointer syntax; otherwise the claim lookup target changes.
Numeric sentinel semantics: value 0 does NOT mean strict zero leeway; it selects the default 60 seconds. Value -1 disables this extra leeway. Never assume 0 disables skew tolerance.

Numeric sentinel semantics: value 0 does NOT mean strict zero leeway; it selects the default 150 seconds. Value -1 disables this extra leeway. For expired_token tests, do not use 0 expecting strict expiry enforcement.

bound_subject supports EXACT string match only; there is no companion type parameter. Wildcards like '*' are treated as literal characters. For I4 multi-identity tests, OMIT bound_subject entirely rather than setting a wildcard.
bound_claims keys may use JSON Pointer syntax, but value matching semantics are controlled only by bound_claims_type. In default string mode, values are treated as literals and must match exactly.

Matching modes: 'string' = exact literal match only; 'glob' = wildcard matching with '*' over strings. For I4 multi-identity scenarios that need multiple distinct values to pass the same claim constraint, either omit the exact-match constraint or intentionally use glob mode; do not set exact-match values to '*'.

For I5 numeric coercion tests, set bound_claims_type to glob, not the default string. The docs state default string mode treats values as literals and exact matches, while glob mode interprets values as globs; use glob mode when testing whether non-string JWT claim values are coerced to strings instead of being rejected outright.
groups_claim must resolve to a LIST OF STRINGS. Do not use a scalar string groups claim when testing group alias mapping; type mismatch will fail before authorization-binding behavior is exercised.

For jwt_default_role_change I3 tests, login requests MUST omit the role parameter so the mount's default_role is actually exercised. If role is sent explicitly, changing default_role has no effect and the test is invalid.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a control login using a valid JWT in the same scenario. Without a control, a failed attack login cannot be distinguished from broken trust-anchor or role setup.

Do NOT treat replay_same_token or stateless_jwt_no_jti as vulnerabilities for Vault JWT auth. JWT bearer replay protection via jti tracking is not documented here and is not expected for stateless JWT verification.

Public OIDC clients MUST use PKCE in the authorization code flow. Confidential clients may use PKCE but are not required to. For PKCE enforcement tests, ensure the client_type under test is public when expecting code_verifier to be mandatory.
The openid scope is required at the authorization endpoint. Do not omit openid in OIDC flow tests or the request is invalid by design.

Vault's OIDC provider docs say nonce is optional but strongly encouraged and it is returned in the ID token nonce claim. For OIDC replay-oriented tests, always send a nonce so the resulting ID token can be checked for nonce binding.

redirect_uri at the token endpoint must exactly match the redirect_uri used when the authorization code was generated. For redirect_uri_mismatch tests, a rejection is by design and should be asserted via status/result, not identity comparison.

client_id is required for public clients and for confidential clients using client_secret_post. client_secret is required for confidential clients using client_secret_post. Alternatively, confidential clients may authenticate with Authorization: Basic using client_secret_basic.

code_verifier is required for authorization codes granted using PKCE and required for public clients. For PKCE tests, absence of code_verifier should be evaluated as flow rejection, not as an identity mix-up.
OIDC provider allowed_client_ids has special semantics: empty means NO clients are allowed; '*' means all clients are allowed. Do not use an empty list expecting wildcard behavior.

OIDC client assignments default to denying all Vault entities. To allow authentication through the client, configure assignments explicitly, e.g. the built-in allow_all assignment, or a specific assignment resource. Otherwise OIDC flow failures may be caused by client assignment denial rather than the invariant under test.
redirect_uris must exactly match the redirect_uri used in each authentication request. Do not use wildcard or prefix assumptions; mismatch failures are by design.
client_type and key cannot be modified after client creation. If a test needs to change public vs confidential behavior or signing key, create a fresh client instead of attempting in-place mutation.
id_token_ttl should be less than the signing key's verification_ttl. If id_token_ttl exceeds verification_ttl, downstream validation windows may not behave as expected during key-rotation tests.

Numeric sentinel semantics on named-key rotation: when rotating a named key, verification_ttl=0 overrides to literal zero additional verification retention for the rotated key material per the sample payload semantics. Do not assume 0 means 'use default' here; test key-rotation timing carefully.
Vault KV v2 read paths MUST include /data/ in the URL. Using the mount root without /data/ hits the wrong API shape and causes false 404/permission results.

Token lookup-self consumes the session token like any other authenticated API call. If the issued token has a limited use budget (for example token_num_uses on the auth role or num_uses on token creation), verify_granted_identity will decrement it before verify_read_secret. Minimum safe value for a sequence that does both self-lookup and secret-read is at least 2 uses, and at least 3 if an additional entity lookup is performed.

Numeric sentinel semantics: token_num_uses/num_uses value 0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. Any positive value counts EVERY authenticated API call, including verification calls in the verify phase.

External-vs-internal group semantics matter for authorization tests. Group aliases are the documented mechanism for mapping external group names into identity groups; use create_group_alias rather than trying to simulate external group membership only with manual member_entity_ids when testing JWT/OIDC group claims.

Group policy application mode affects whether identity group policies apply only within namespace hierarchy or across any namespace. For I5 group_policy_escalation tests in Enterprise, record the current mode because 'any' can legitimately broaden where group policies apply across namespaces.

configure_jwt_validation requires exactly one trust source among oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, and jwt_validation_pubkeys. The fuzzer MUST set exactly one of these and MUST NOT combine them, or setup is invalid.

create_auth_role requires at least one bound value to be set. The fuzzer MUST provide at least one of bound_audiences, bound_subject, or bound_claims (or other documented bound values) or role creation is invalid.

For JWT roles, bound_audiences is required when the JWT contains an aud claim (typical case) and must match at least one JWT aud value. For I5 audience tests, include a control token with matching aud and an attack token with mismatched aud; otherwise failures may be caused by missing baseline configuration.

bound_claims matching semantics are controlled by bound_claims_type. Default bound_claims_type='string' means literal exact matching; glob wildcards only work when bound_claims_type='glob'. For I4 multi-identity scenarios, exact-match bound_claims entries MUST be omitted rather than set to '*'.

bound_claims accepts string, integer, boolean, or list-of-strings expected values. Because default bound_claims_type='string' treats values as literals and exact matches, the fuzzer SHOULD run I5 numeric coercion tests with bound_claims_type='glob' so numeric JWT claim values are coerced to strings rather than rejected outright.

groups_claim must resolve to a list of strings. Sending a scalar string instead of a list can fail type validation rather than exercising group alias mapping logic. For I4 type-confusion-groups tests, distinguish parser rejection from identity-collision behavior.

user_claim must resolve to a string. If user_claim_json_pointer=false (default), the value is interpreted literally as a claim name, not a JSON pointer. For nested claims, the fuzzer MUST set user_claim_json_pointer=true or the wrong claim will be read.

Numeric sentinel semantics on JWT leeway fields: clock_skew_leeway value 0 means use default 60 seconds, not literal zero; value -1 disables extra leeway. expiration_leeway value 0 means use default 150 seconds, not literal zero; value -1 disables extra leeway. not_before_leeway value 0 means use default 150 seconds, not literal zero; value -1 disables extra leeway. Never assume 0 means strict checking.

Session-use budget: token_num_uses on JWT/OIDC roles limits every API call made with the issued Vault token, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the sequence performs both self-lookup and secret-read, minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use >=3 if additional session-inspection calls are included.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests on JWT login, include a control login using a valid token alongside the attack token. Otherwise LOGIN_FAILED may reflect broken trust configuration rather than time-claim enforcement.

For I1 issuer-validation tests against JWT login, configure_jwt_validation MUST include bound_issuer. If bound_issuer is omitted, Vault will not compare iss against a configured value and the test becomes non-diagnostic.

For I1 signing-key-rotation tests, update configure_jwt_validation trust material (jwks_url or jwt_validation_pubkeys) and then retry the old JWT. A successful login after rotation indicates stale trust; a successful login because the admin intentionally changed trust anchors is by design only for the new key.

For I3 default-role-change tests, login_with_jwt may omit role and then uses default_role from mount config. To test coherence, the fuzzer MUST omit role on both baseline and post-change logins; specifying role bypasses default_role entirely.

OIDC auth_url/callback flow coherence: client_nonce supplied to /auth/{mount}/oidc/auth_url must match client_nonce on /auth/{mount}/oidc/callback if used. The fuzzer MUST preserve state, nonce, and optional client_nonce from the same flow instance; cross-session swaps are expected to fail.

Vault's OIDC auth_url endpoint returns a generated auth_url rather than acting as the authorization endpoint itself. The fuzzer MUST treat this as a two-step brokered flow and preserve the returned state/nonce values for the callback test.
Vault OIDC provider authorization endpoint requires scope to include 'openid'. Requests without openid are invalid and should not be interpreted as security rejections.

Vault OIDC provider clients: public clients must use PKCE for authorization code flow; confidential clients may use PKCE optionally. For PKCE-related tests, configure client_type accordingly or failures may be due to client-type requirements rather than binding behavior.

OIDC provider redirect_uris must exactly match the redirect_uri used in authorization and token requests. For redirect_uri mismatch tests, ensure the baseline uses an exact configured URI; otherwise all exchanges fail for setup reasons.

OIDC provider assignments default to allowing no Vault entities. To permit authentication through a client, the fuzzer MUST configure assignments (for example allow_all or a specific assignment). Otherwise authorization/token issuance failures are by configuration, not security checks.

OIDC provider allowed_client_ids on the provider defaults to allowing no clients when empty; '*' allows all clients. For cross-client/provider audience tests, explicitly configure allowed_client_ids so failures are attributable to audience/client binding rather than provider deny-by-default behavior.

OIDC provider token endpoint in the provided docs supports only grant_type=authorization_code. Do NOT treat this endpoint as RFC 8693 token exchange support; token_exchange attacks are not supported by the documented Vault OIDC provider API.

OIDC provider discovery explicitly reports request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false. Do NOT run oidc_request_object_alg_none tests against this provider API; unsigned request-object acceptance is not applicable to the documented endpoint.

OIDC provider discovery shows token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported includes client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, and none. The fuzzer MUST match client authentication method to client_type and request style; sending client_secret for a public client or omitting required client auth for a confidential client causes expected failures.

For OIDC SSO validation strategy, nonce is documented as optional but strongly encouraged on the provider authorization endpoint. When testing replay resistance or OIDC id_token validation, the fuzzer SHOULD include nonce in control flows; absence of nonce may weaken the oracle because the platform may legitimately omit nonce-based checks when none was requested.
KV v2 pathing: verify_read_secret and seed_protected_resource MUST use /v1/{engine}/data/{path}. Omitting /data/ hits the wrong API shape and returns 404 unrelated to authorization.

Identity group alias testing: external JWT/OIDC groups are mapped through group aliases using mount_accessor plus alias name. For group-policy escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST create the internal group, then create a group alias with the auth mount accessor, and ensure groups_claim emits a list of matching alias names.

Identity entity alias names are security-sensitive. Vault docs warn that multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias and thereby share privileges. For I4 collision tests, alias reuse is a real risk surface, not merely cosmetic naming.

Group policy application mode can be 'within_namespace_hierarchy' (default) or 'any'. For I5 group-policy tests in multi-namespace environments, the fuzzer MUST account for this global setting or cross-namespace policy inheritance results may be by design.
